headline: US midterms spark bigger clash over data centers, with new limits expected
summary: Voters' anger over data centers became a political force in the recent US midterms, with over 80% opposing local builds. This could lead to congressional action on construction and community say.
details: The recent US midterm elections have given Democrats full control of Congress, potentially leading to one of the most divided governments in decades. These results highlight growing public anger over data centers, the massive facilities powering AI, as a significant political force.

An NBC exit poll revealed that over half of respondents believe AI will do more harm than good, and nearly 80% are against data center construction in their communities. Almost 60% considered data centers a crucial factor in their vote, with one racial justice organization calling the election a referendum on economic beneficiaries.

This anti-data center sentiment was particularly strong in states like Ohio, where OpenAI has considered a $500 billion data center project backed by Nvidia. A county in Ohio, where Meta had planned a large facility, recently passed a ban on data centers, and local communities statewide overwhelmingly rejected related buildout measures.

Analysts at Morgan Stanley predict that Ohio's Democratic Governor-elect Amy Acton will pose a major risk to the state's data center expansion. Similarly, candidates in Texas, Maine, Michigan, Nevada, Georgia, and South Carolina won seats after campaigning against rapid data center development, demonstrating that campaign spending doesn't always guarantee outcomes.

Future actions could include more construction moratoriums or requirements for data centers to fund their own power grid upgrades, preventing costs from being passed to local communities. Goldman Sachs forecasts construction delays in states like Georgia and Texas due to Democratic gains.

Democratic control of Congress could also boost bills like the one proposed by Sen. Bernie Sanders and Rep. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez. This bill suggests a nationwide moratorium on new data centers until Congress establishes guardrails to prevent increased electricity costs, environmental harm, or construction without community consent.

Other legislative efforts, such as New Mexico Sen. Martin Heinrich's GRID Savings Act, aim to prevent communities from bearing grid infrastructure costs during large AI data center expansions. Environmental concerns are also prominent, particularly regarding gas turbine-powered facilities like xAI's in Memphis and those across Virginia.

Experts believe changes to energy regulations, land rights, and environmental policies could significantly impact data center development, especially as congressional Democrats revisit Trump-era energy protection rollbacks. State and local movements are also expected to continue, with examples like Texas Gov.-elect Gina Hinojosa supporting a statewide moratorium.

headline: X web app loads 8x faster, showing first post in 2.7 seconds, rolling out globally
summary: The updated app reduces load time from over 22 seconds to 2.7 seconds for signed-in users, rolling out country by country.
details: X is rolling out a new version of its web app that promises significantly faster loading times. Principal engineer Yagiz Nizipli stated that on slow connections, the first post now appears in 2.7 seconds, down from over 22 seconds on the old app.

This represents an 8x improvement in initial content display. The rollout is happening "one country at a time" for signed-in users, but the rewrite is already active for logged-out experiences and search engine crawlers.

Technically, the updated app replaces three separate servers previously used for people, search crawlers, and link previews with a single, more efficient system. This consolidation contributes to the overall speed gains and streamlined operation.

Security researcher Jane Manchun Wong, who gained early access, confirmed the improvements, describing the app as "snappy, loads fast and many parts are polished." This user feedback aligns with X's official claims regarding performance.
